title: 春日偶成
author: 程颢
intro: A serious philosopher takes a stroll on a mild spring day and feels quietly happy — and jokes that people will think he is just a middle-aged man playing truant like a schoolboy.
analysis: 这首诗是《千家诗》的第一首，很多中国孩子从它开始读古诗。前两句写春天中午的好天气：云很淡，风很轻，诗人靠着花、跟着柳树，走过前面的小河。“傍”和“随”两个动词，写出他悠闲散步、被春景吸引的样子。后两句写心情：路上的人不懂我心里的快乐，还以为我是在偷懒，学年轻人出来玩呢。作者程颢是有名的理学家（研究“理”的哲学家），平时很严肃。他的快乐不只是看风景，而是在自然中体会到一种自在和谐的心境。诗里有一点自嘲的幽默：大学者也有像孩子一样贪玩的时候。语言平易，像随口说出来的，题目“偶成”就是“偶然写成”的意思。
analysisEn: This poem opens the Poems by a Thousand Masters (Qiānjiā Shī), an old children’s primer, so for generations it was the first classical poem many Chinese children read. The first two lines describe a perfect spring noon: thin clouds, a light breeze, and the poet strolling beside the flowers, following the willows, across the stream ahead. The two verbs 傍 (“keeping close to”) and 随 (“following”) show him wandering at leisure, drawn along by the scenery. The last two lines turn to his feelings: people he passes don’t understand the joy in his heart — they probably think he’s skiving off, trying to act young again. Cheng Hao was a famous Neo-Confucian philosopher, known as a serious thinker. His happiness is not just about pretty views; it is the calm, natural joy of feeling in tune with the world. There is a touch of self-mocking humour too: even a great scholar can feel like a boy skipping school. The language is plain, almost offhand — the title 偶成 means “written on the spur of the moment”.
background: Cheng Hao (1032–1085) was a Northern Song philosopher who, with his younger brother Cheng Yi, laid the foundations of Neo-Confucianism. He is said to have written this while serving as a local official.
pronunciation: 傍花：傍 bàng（靠近）。过前川：过 guò。余心乐：乐 lè。将谓：将 jiāng。少年：少 shào。
version: 采用通行教材版本（《千家诗》卷首）。“余心乐”一作“予心乐”（余、予都是“我”）；“时人”有本作“旁人”。网站用教材版。

lines.py: yún dàn fēng qīng jìn wǔ tiān
lines.lit: Clouds pale, wind light, the sky near noon;
lines.en: Thin clouds, a soft breeze, nearly noon —

lines.py: bàng huā suí liǔ guò qián chuān
lines.lit: beside the flowers, following the willows, I cross the stream ahead.
lines.en: I stroll by the flowers, follow the willows across the stream.

lines.py: shí rén bù shí yú xīn lè
lines.lit: People of the day don’t know the joy in my heart;
lines.en: Passers-by can’t see the happiness inside me —

lines.py: jiāng wèi tōu xián xué shào nián
lines.lit: they will say I steal leisure, imitating a youth.
lines.en: they’ll think I’m playing truant, pretending to be young.

words.note: 偶：偶然，现代汉语“偶然”“偶尔”。
今天常说“云淡风轻”，也比喻心态平和、不在乎。
现代汉语“中午”“午饭”的“午”。
现代汉语“依山傍水”；“傍晚”也是这个字。
古义；现代汉语多用在地名和成语里，如“四川”“川流不息”。
古代第一人称，现代汉语说“我”。
现代汉语仍用，如“忙里偷闲”。

imagery.name: 云
imagery.zh: 淡淡的云写出春日晴朗，也映出诗人淡然平和的心境。
imagery.en: Thin clouds show a clear spring day — and mirror the poet’s calm, easy mood.

imagery.name: 风
imagery.zh: 轻风拂面，春天的舒适让人想出门走走。
imagery.en: A light breeze makes the day so pleasant that you just want to go for a walk.

imagery.name: 花
imagery.zh: “傍花”——靠着花走，写出春天的美和诗人的流连。
imagery.en: Walking close to the flowers: spring’s beauty, and the poet lingering in it.

imagery.name: 柳
imagery.zh: “随柳”——沿着柳树走，柳色引着人一路前行。
imagery.en: Following the willows: the fresh green leads him on along the stream.
